articles.title: Anthropic Runs 30,000 Agents at Once. What Keeps Them Under Control?
articles.excerpt: In one of Anthropic's internal experiments, a group of Claude agents was supposed to solve math problems. Some of them started killing each other's processes instead. The agents had accidentally been…
articles.body: In one of Anthropic's internal experiments, a group of Claude agents was supposed to solve math problems. Some of them started killing each other's processes instead. The agents had accidentally been launched into a shared working directory. They competed over files, utilities, and API rate limits. According to Anthropic's August 2026 Risk Report , many Claude Mythos 5 agents independently terminated other agents' processes while trying to avoid being terminated themselves. Anthropic describes the incident as arising in a broken agent scaffold, rather than attributing it to a jailbreak or malicious task instruction. Anyone who has dealt with conflicting processes, shared state, or poorly isolated CI jobs will recognize the underlying infrastructure problem.
articles.author: Bargan Constantin

articles.title: Swift vs SwiftUI vs Flutter: Which Is Right for Your iPhone App in the UAE?
articles.excerpt: Choosing a technology is one of the first decisions in an iPhone project, and it is often confused. Swift, SwiftUI and Flutter are not three competing options of the same kind. Understanding what each…
articles.body: Choosing a technology is one of the first decisions in an iPhone project, and it is often confused. Swift, SwiftUI and Flutter are not three competing options of the same kind. Understanding what each one is makes the decision much easier. What Each One Actually Is Swift is Apple’s programming language for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS and visionOS. SwiftUI is Apple’s modern framework for building user interfaces, written in Swift. Its older counterpart is UIKit. Flutter is Google’s cross-platform framework, written in Dart, that builds iOS and Android apps from one codebase. So the real comparison is between a native iOS approach (Swift with SwiftUI or UIKit) and a cross-platform approach (Flutter).

articles.title: I’m building Meith: forum software with a modern stack
articles.excerpt: There’s something useful about a forum thread that’s still answering people’s questions five years after someone started it. The original problem is there. So are the suggestions, the things that didn…
articles.body: There’s something useful about a forum thread that’s still answering people’s questions five years after someone started it. The original problem is there. So are the suggestions, the things that didn’t work, and the reply halfway down that actually solved it. Someone arriving later can follow the whole conversation without needing to know who to ask. I think that’s still worth building for. That’s the idea behind Meith , an open-source, self-hosted forum platform I’m working on. It gives a community its own board, on its own domain, with a PostgreSQL database it controls. Threads, search, moderation, private messages and subscriptions are all part of that foundation. But this is DEV, so let’s get into how it’s built, and why.

articles.title: I Built a Website for the Memorial Stone Industry. Here Is What I Learned
articles.excerpt: When I took on the Stone Discover UK project, I assumed it would be a simple catalogue site. Memorial headstones are a niche, and the buyers are not browsing casually. They are monumental masons, fune…
articles.body: When I took on the Stone Discover UK project, I assumed it would be a simple catalogue site. Memorial headstones are a niche, and the buyers are not browsing casually. They are monumental masons, funeral homes and stone retailers who buy in bulk. It turned out to be one of the most useful projects I have worked on, because everything I assumed about "normal" e-commerce was wrong. Here is what I learned. 1. B2B buyers are not B2C shoppers My first instinct was a cart and a checkout. But trade buyers do not add a headstone to a basket and pay. They want to know: Can you supply bulk quantities? What is the lead time? Can you do custom sizes and engraving? Do the products meet cemetery authority requirements? So instead of a checkout, the main call to action became a Get a Quote form.

articles.body: SpacetimeDB's homepage is written for AI agents. Its headline is "Let AI ship the whole backend, glue-free", and the site ships an llms.txt , an agent setup guide, a Claude Code plugin, agent skills, an MCP server built into its CLI, and a public benchmark of how well LLMs write code for it. In our tests, a coding agent built a working, live-updating app on SpacetimeDB with no help from us. It used none of that tooling. And when we asked agents which backend to use for a web app, they picked Convex or Supabase. SpacetimeDB is a database that is also your server, made by Clockwork Labs. We put it through our agent experience (AX) audit, following our AX audit method . The audit has four stages: Awareness: does the model know SpacetimeDB without searching?

articles.title: Your PDF Files Should Never Leave Your Laptop
articles.excerpt: A small experiment I want you to try Take a PDF you actually care about — a contract, a bank statement, a scanned ID. Now go to any of the big "free PDF tools" websites and merge it with something, or…
articles.body: A small experiment I want you to try Take a PDF you actually care about — a contract, a bank statement, a scanned ID. Now go to any of the big "free PDF tools" websites and merge it with something, or compress it, or convert it. Watch what happens. Your file uploads . Somewhere, a progress bar fills while your document travels to a server you've never heard of, in a country you didn't pick, where a copy of it sits for some amount of time you can't verify. Those sites aren't villains. Uploading is just how they were built — ten years ago, browsers were too weak to do serious document work, so the server did it. The model stuck around because it's also convenient for them : your files on their disk, your traffic on their ads, your email on their signup form.

articles.body: Bulkhead is rolling out region locking in multiplayer first-person shooter Wardogs to, in the studio's words, protect "the largest amount of players from an influx of regions that are more prone to cheating." However, legitimate players in Asia have raised concerns, and cross-region players have criticized the developer for blocked from joining their friends. The region lock is done by limiting the maximum ping — the player’s connection with the server — to 175. On paper, this is a fair, non-discriminatory way to stop players from distant regions from entering games with an unstable connection. According to Bulkhead, this would cut down on cheating, too.

articles.body: Capcom has disclosed a data breach of its online membership service affecting over 11 million customer accounts, warning gamers to brace themselves for potential phishing attempts. The Resident Evil, Monster Hunter, and Street Fighter developer said customer information associated with Capcom ID was accessed by a third-party on October 19. 11.7 million email address records were affected globally, exposing date and time of account creation, date and time of last login, number of logins, and the client IP address used during last login. Of these, 43 records of date of birth, gender, country/region, and nickname were affected, and 196 accounts saw unauthorized changes to their Capcom ID login passwords.

articles.body: But if you're looking for an anime that understands how horror can be both visually repulsive and emotionally devastating, Devilman Crybaby is the perfect series for you. Released on Netflix in 2018, Masaaki Yuasa's 10-episode adaptation of Go Nagai's Devilman is a spectacularly gruesome descent into the apocalypse. At its center is Akira Fudo, a sensitive young man forced into a horrific union with a demon to defend humankind from an existential threat. Granted immense power without sacrificing his empathy, Akira becomes a walking paradox: a creature born of unimaginable violence who still weeps for mankind. This core tension that propels the narrative, probing the fragile line between humanity and monstrosity.

articles.title: Faster to Science: A Letter to the Science Community
articles.excerpt: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall.
articles.body: Dear NASA Science Community, NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall, from NASA Headquarters, to explain our new Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), and answer your questions. We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long. It has taken years to move mission concepts through the current two-step process. This has often come with contract management challenges, unpredictability, and not enough funding. NASA is committed to doing better — and I’m excited to share with you how we’re making it happen.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.
